parameters.query: select * from public.note_submissions where status = 'pending_extraction' order by created_at limit 1;

update public.note_submissions
set status = 'processing', claimed_at = now(), attempts = attempts + 1
where id = $1 and status = 'pending_extraction'
returning *;
update public.note_submissions set status = 'completed', skipped = $1, error = null, processed_at = now() where id = $2 returning id;
update public.note_submissions set status = 'failed', error = $1, processed_at = now() where id = $2 returning id;
update public.note_submissions set status = $1, skipped = $2, error = $3, processed_at = now() where id = $4 returning id, status;

parameters.content:
## pipeline-note-extraction
The n8n replacement for local-agent/agent.mjs noteLoop. Introduces the 'POST per extracted item to an Edge Function' pattern the plan flags as needed later for photos (pipeline-process-cards, Stage 4).

Find Pending Note + Claim Note Submission mirror findNextPendingNoteSubmission/claimNoteSubmission exactly: a plain SELECT to pick a candidate, then a single UPDATE ... WHERE status=pending_extraction RETURNING * as the actual atomic claim. If Claim returns 0 rows (another overlapping execution claimed it first between the SELECT and the UPDATE), the chain simply stops here -- zero-item safety, no explicit IF needed -- exactly the same safe race local-agent already tolerates.

Has Contacts? branches BEFORE the posting loop rather than relying on zero-item behavior after it, on purpose: a note with zero extracted contacts is 'a valid, expected result, not a failure' per the skill's own docs, and it must still write a completed row with the skipped list -- deriving that from an empty-input aggregate step risked the aggregate never running at all (n8n skips downstream nodes when a node returns 0 items). Branching upfront sidesteps the ambiguity entirely.

Prepare Contacts For Posting reads noteSubmissionId/skipped from upstream ONCE, while it still has exactly one input item, and stamps them onto every fanned-out per-contact item -- deliberately not re-read via $('Claim Note Submission').item after the fan-out, since a Code node emitting multiple new items does not preserve n8n's pairedItem linking back to a single upstream item unambiguously.

Post To Contacts From Note posts one at a time (not batched), same reasoning as postExtractedContact: a single unusable entry costs only itself. onError continueErrorOutput + Record Success/Record Failure normalize both outcomes into one shape before Aggregate Results (a Code node in runOnceForAllItems mode) computes created/failures -- since Has Contacts? already guarantees at least one item reaches this branch, no splitInBatches/onDone machinery is needed to guarantee the aggregate step runs.

Partial success stays 'completed' with failures recorded in error -- only a note where NOTHING could be created is 'failed'. Matches processNoteSubmission's allFailed logic exactly: the contacts that did land are already real and visible in Review.

The Supabase Service Role (n8n) credential here is a genuinely new one (Authorization: Bearer <service-role-key> only, per supabase/functions/_shared/auth.ts isServiceRoleCall) -- distinct from Stage 0's Supabase Storage (n8n) credential, which needs a different header template (apikey + Authorization together) for the Storage REST API. Same underlying secret value, two different httpTemplatedCustomAuth credential definitions, since the header template is baked into the credential type itself. Reusable as-is for contacts-from-ocr in Stage 4.

This is the parent orchestrating workflow, not a skill sub-workflow -- holding the Supabase write credential here (after schema-validation success, never inside a skill sub-workflow) is exactly the credential model the plan specifies.

INACTIVE / BUILD-ONLY (n8n migration Stage 2). No credential is actually attached yet -- see n8n/README.md.
